content.text:
`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes all 7 tests. I made two code fixes in `household/bills.py` and changed one test.

**Code fixes:**
1. **`split_bill`** dropped the leftover cents, so the shares didn't add up to the total: 1001 split 2 ways gave `[500, 500]`. It now uses `divmod` and gives one extra cent to each of the first people, which is what the docstring describes. 1001 split 2 ways now gives `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates`** never moved to the next year, so any series running past December crashed with "bad month number 13". It now wraps the month and increases the year when it passes December.

**Test change (please check this one):** in `tests/test_bills.py`, `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3) == [333, 333, 333]`. Those shares add up to 999, not 1000, so the test contradicted both the docstring and the remainder test. No version of `split_bill` could pass both tests. I changed the expected result to `[334, 333, 333]` because the docstring says the cents must add up exactly. If you'd rather lose the remainder, the code and docstring need to change instead, and `test_remainder_goes_to_the_first` would then be the wrong test.

Nothing is committed.
